abstract: We propose and experimentally validate a keyword wake-up approach based on an all-optical nonlinear diffractive deep neural network (AON-D2NN) chip. The chip monolithically integrates an input layer, nine hidden layers, and an output layer. The hidden layers employ thermal phase shifter arrays for programmable matrix operations, and germanium microstructures provide on-chip nonlinear activation functions. We preprocess speech signals via fast Fourier transform (FFT) and intensity sampling at characteristic frequencies, then encode them into voltage vectors for parallel input. Using the stochastic gradient descent algorithm for in-situ training in the optical domain, we achieve a recognition accuracy of 75% in a binary classification task with the AON-D2NN chip. Benefiting from the all-optical forward propagation architecture, the chip avoids frequent photoelectric conversions and reduces its computation latency to 172 ps. This work offers a viable solution for low-power and low-latency optical-domain speech recognition.
title: All-optical speech recognition based on nonlinear diffractive neural network with picosecond latency

abstract: ABSTRACT Diffractive deep neural networks (D 2 NNs) offer a promising route toward high‐speed wave‐based computing, but most existing architectures are restricted to a single fixed function, whereas multitask implementations often require additional hardware complexity. Here, a multitask D 2 NN architecture based on joint distance and frequency encoding is proposed and demonstrated. The interlayer distance is introduced as a physically reconfigurable task‐encoding dimension and is combined with a dual‐frequency phase‐independent metasurface to enable task multiplexing within a single passive hardware system. Scalar diffraction simulations on the corresponding testing datasets yielded accuracies of 99.7% for 9‐class orbital angular momentum (OAM) classification, 86.4% for 9‐class direction recognition, 98.8% for 4‐category programmable logic‐gate operations, and 95.4% for 4‐class MNIST digit recognition (Digits 0–3). Full‐wave electromagnetic simulations further support the physical feasibility of the designed metasurface implementation, whereas microwave measurements on selected representative inputs provide proof‐of‐concept evidence of task‐dependent energy routing and distance‐enabled task switching. This joint‐encoding strategy provides a compact and resource‐efficient route for multifunctional intelligent wave‐based computing systems.
title: Multitask Diffractive Deep Neural Networks Enabled by Joint Distance–Frequency Encoding
